findings.title: Legacy folder=assistant.name chats are not merged into the Assistant Folder group
findings.problem: getFolderKey treats any truthy chat.folder as a Custom Folder unconditionally (`if (chat.folder) return customFolderKey(chat.folder)`), with no check against the assistant's name. The identical pattern exists in focusedChatSidebarCollections.ts's collectFocusedChats (`if (chat.folder) { addToFolder(...); continue }` runs before the assistant-identity fallback). Spec §3.3.3 requires an `isAssistantNameFolder(chat, assistants)` helper so a chat.folder that equals the assistant's name falls through to Assistant Folder classification instead (§2.1 step 5 explicitly excludes assistant-name folders from Custom Folder, per the isCustomFolder(...) pseudocode) — this helper does not exist anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms zero matches for isAssistantNameFolder or isCustomFolder).
findings.impact: Any pre-existing chat whose folder still equals its assistant's name — exactly the historical 'folder pollution' this ticket's Goal #2 exists to fix — renders as a duplicate, spurious Custom Folder named after the assistant, instead of being grouped with that assistant's real Assistant Folder entry. The sidebar shows the same assistant's chats split across two different groups.
findings.recommendation: Add isAssistantNameFolder(chat, assistants) (or reuse the already-resolved assistant identity from getAssistantIdentity) and check it before the `if (chat.folder) return customFolderKey(...)` branch in both unifiedChatSidebarViewModel.ts's getFolderKey and focusedChatSidebarCollections.ts's collectFocusedChats, so a folder-name-equals-assistant-name match falls through to assistant-folder classification instead of custom-folder classification.

findings.title: Sidebar chat name no longer masks the optimistic name while a rename is pending
findings.problem: getChatDisplayName now returns chat.name.trim() whenever it is non-empty, with no check of a pending-rename flag. At the branch's merge-base, the equivalent logic was `if (chat.name?.trim() && !chat.pendingRename) chatName = chat.name.trim()`. `pendingRename` was removed from the ChatListItem interface in this diff, but src/store/chatGeneration.ts still actively sets/clears it via `chatsStore.updateChatListItem({ id, pendingRename: true/false })` at lines 576, 591 and 612 — these calls still compile only because TypeScript's excess-property check does not reliably fire through the `Partial<ChatListItem> & { id: string }` intersection parameter type, silently masking the type/behavior mismatch.
findings.impact: During the LLM-generated-name polling window (EPMCDME-11647), the sidebar now flashes the raw truncated first-message optimistic name instead of holding a placeholder, because the UI-layer guard that used to read pendingRename was dropped while the store-layer plumbing that sets it remains fully intact and tested — chatGeneration.renamePoll.test.ts still passes because it only asserts store state, never the rendered chat name.
findings.recommendation: Reintroduce a pendingRename (or equivalently named) field on ChatListItem and check it in getChatDisplayName (ChatListItem.tsx), the same way the pre-existing code did, so the render path is reconnected to the store flag chatGeneration.ts already maintains.
